question: A director tells a service manager to "roll Claude out across the department next quarter." The department runs eleven distinct workflows of varying sensitivity. What should the service manager do first?
options: A) Ask Claude to review all eleven workflows and recommend which of them to change first.
B) Draft a departmental policy covering how Claude may be used in each of the eleven workflows.
C) Give every team access at the start of the quarter so that people can begin finding uses for it.
D) Choose one workflow and one outcome to improve, and agree how that will be measured.
correct_answers: D) Choose one workflow and one outcome to improve, and agree how that will be measured.
explanations: Claude can help compare the workflows once someone describes them, but it cannot know which of them the department most needs to fix or which carry unacceptable risk. Handing the prioritisation over skips the manager's own judgment.
A usage policy will be needed eventually, particularly for the sensitive workflows. Writing it for all eleven before anything has been attempted means guessing at the practices it should govern.

Broad access with no chosen target produces scattered experiments across eleven workflows, including the sensitive ones. At the end of the quarter the manager will have activity to report but no evidence of improvement.

Correct. A vague rollout instruction becomes deliverable by narrowing it to one workflow and one measurable outcome. That gives a bounded first integration, a clear basis for judging whether it worked, and evidence to take back to the director before spreading further.
